name: Tianjin Binhai International Airport
before:
Tianjin's airport, and one of China's major air cargo centres. It handled 19,862,196 passengers in 2025, twenty sixth in the country, and is the hub for Tianjin Airlines and Okay Airways with Air China treating it as a focus city.

The metro makes the transfer easy and cheap. Binhai International Airport station on Line 2 has served the terminal since August 2014 and the fare downtown is three yuan.

The terminal is a good deal bigger than it was. The current building went up in 2006 and was expanded around 2010 to 116,000 square metres, more than three times the size of the one before it, with 47 jet bridges.

This is also where Airbus builds. The A320 final assembly line opened here in 2008 and the A330 completion and delivery centre was finished at the end of 2017.

For the 2025 winter and spring season the airport planned 120 routes serving 97 cities.
after: Tianjin's airport, the 26th busiest in China with 19.9 million passengers in 2025. Tianjin Airlines and Okay Airways both have their home base here.

claims.claim: one of China's major air cargo centres; exact figure; Air China focus city
claims.wasBefore: Tianjin's airport, and one of China's major air cargo centres. It handled 19,862,196 passengers in 2025, twenty sixth in the country, and is the hub for Tianjin Airlines and Okay Airways with Air China treating it as a focus city.
claims.why: CAAC's 2025 table puts Tianjin 30th in China for cargo (133,023 tonnes), which does not support 'major cargo centre'; Wikipedia says 26th for cargo, so the sources disagree anyway. Air China's focus city rests on Wikipedia alone.

claims.claim: metro Line 2 since August 2014; three yuan downtown
claims.wasBefore: The metro makes the transfer easy and cheap. Binhai International Airport station on Line 2 has served the terminal since August 2014 and the fare downtown is three yuan.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone. Tianjin Metro's own site could not be read (tjgdjt.com answered 502 and 405; tjdt.cn is not the metro's site) and a fare needs a source from the last 12 months.

claims.claim: 2006 terminal expanded around 2010 to 116,000 m2, 47 jet bridges
claims.wasBefore: The terminal is a good deal bigger than it was. The current building went up in 2006 and was expanded around 2010 to 116,000 square metres, more than three times the size of the one before it, with 47 jet bridges.
claims.why: Describes the building before Terminal 2, which came into use on 28 August 2014 (Wikipedia); single source throughout.

claims.claim: Airbus A320 final assembly line 2008; A330 completion centre end of 2017
claims.wasBefore: This is also where Airbus builds. The A320 final assembly line opened here in 2008 and the A330 completion and delivery centre was finished at the end of 2017.
claims.why: Wikipedia alone in the saved sources. airbus.com answers with an Imperva bot check, which the sweep does not try to get round.

claims.claim: 2025 winter and spring season: 120 routes, 97 cities
claims.wasBefore: For the 2025 winter and spring season the airport planned 120 routes serving 97 cities.
claims.why: Confirmed by Sina Finance (19 Oct 2025) and Wikipedia, but that season ended on 28 March 2026.
